The default lifetime of local variables in a PHP function is from the time the variable is first used (i.e., when storage for it is allocated) until the function's execution terminates. The lifetime of a static variable in a function begins when the variable is first used in the first execution of the function. Its lifetime ends when the script execution ends. In PHP, a local variable in a function can be specified to be static by declaring it with the reserved word static. <?phpfunction myTest() { static x; $x++;}myTest();myTest();myTest();?>
Then, each time the function is called, that variable will still have the information it contained from the last time the function was called.
